title: opum-lore pane: no auto-start in teammate, headless or workflow processes; once-registered, in-flight-guarded clocks
description:
Filed by lore-cli's session from opum-doc DEC-172 (4bg), the design ruling relayed via team-lead on 2026-10-12; item 2 of that ruling's per-repository spec is the binding scope for lore-cli.

Context: a host load incident on 2026-10-12 (DEC-172 (4bg) records host load 128/225/269 at 03:07:43Z). Mod clocks ran in every Claude process - teammates, headless and workflow processes alike. The opum-lore pane auto-opens on session.start and refreshes every 30s, and its refresh has NO in-flight guard (lore findings B1 and B2); there is no session.end handler, so no timer is ever cancelled (B3). There is NO fleet mode in opum-lore to remove: the "Refs" view reads refs in its own repository, so only the auto-start gate and the clock hardening apply.

Operator's first-party ruling, recorded verbatim in DEC-172 (4bg): "teammates, and dynamic workflows should not be running the mode automatically".

Scope (DEC-172 (4bg) item 2, HIGH): implement lore-cli's items (b), (c) and (e) as written, plus an in-flight guard on refresh. Item (a) - removing fleet mode - does not apply, because opum-lore has none. Not campaign work.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Auto-start gate: on session.start, when !e.isInteractive OR $.env.get("CLAUDECODE") === "1", open no pane and register no clock. An explicit open by the person still works and polls only while shown.

Every clock is registered once per process (a module guard), its handle is kept, and it is cancelled at session.end. Each WHOLE clock callback is guarded in flight, skipping a tick while the previous one runs. The refresh gets its own in-flight guard as well.
Every subprocess has a timeout, and no tick spawns more than 3 processes.

Proof both ways: a CLAUDECODE=1 process, and one with isInteractive false, each spawn 0 lore/git children over 5 minutes; an interactive process stays within the bound; a soak of 8 interactive processes for 10 minutes shows no growth in child processes, with the counts reported; and claude plugin validate lists the env read.

implementationNotes:
Implemented DEC-172 (4bg) item 2 for the opum-lore pane (hooks/register.tsx).

Gate (AC1): session.start computes `gated = !e.isInteractive || (await $.env.get("CLAUDECODE")) === "1"`. A gated process opens no pane, registers no clock, and does not resolve the root or run the initial read-back, so it spawns ZERO children. A non-gated process does all of it as before. The explicit-open paths (the dashboard tool and the band's button) call ensureClock, so a person's open in a gated process still works and polls from then on.

Clock (AC2): ensureClock registers the one `$.clock.every` clock per process behind a module guard (`refreshTimer`), the Timer handle is kept, a new session.end hook cancels it, the WHOLE tick callback is guarded in flight (`tickInFlight`) so a slow period skips its tick rather than stacking, and it polls refresh+countUncommitted only while the pane is SHOWN. refresh is single-flight (`refreshInFlight`).

Subprocesses (AC3): all three `$.process.run` sites already carry `timeoutMs: 30000`; a tick runs exactly three children (refresh's two `lore` reads plus countUncommitted's one `git status`).

Proof (AC4), tests/lcli705.test.ts in the mod kit: an isInteractive:false session and a CLAUDECODE=1 session each spawn ZERO children at start and across a five-minute advance; an interactive session's tick is exactly three; a ten-minute soak stays at three a period (60 over twenty periods); session.end cancels so a later period runs nothing; eight session.starts in one process run ONE clock (three a period, not twenty-four). `claude plugin validate` lists `env reads: CLAUDECODE`.

Gate counts: `bun run test:mod` 66 pass / 0 fail with the mod typecheck clean; `bun test` 5004 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lore check` (exit 0) all green.

Modelling note for the soak: the engine test kit runs one engine process, so "8 interactive processes" is modelled as eight sessions sharing this module (one clock, three children a period) plus a ten-minute soak. The PER-PROCESS bound is what fixes eight real processes at three a period each, not twenty-four; a real interactive soak is not scriptable in CI (interactive sessions cannot be driven headlessly).
finalSummary: Implemented DEC-172 (4bg) item 2 for the opum-lore pane. hooks/register.tsx: session.start gates on `!e.isInteractive || $.env.get("CLAUDECODE") === "1"` (no pane, no clock, no root resolve, no initial read-back, so no child); the refresh clock is registered once per process behind a module guard, its Timer handle kept, the whole tick guarded in flight, refresh single-flight, and the handle cancelled at session.end; an explicit open still opens and polls. tests/lcli705.test.ts proves zero children for a non-interactive and a CLAUDECODE=1 session over five minutes, three children a tick for an interactive one, a ten-minute soak within the bound, session.end cancellation, and one clock across eight sessions. `claude plugin validate` lists `env reads: CLAUDECODE`. Gates: test:mod 66 pass / 0 fail (mod typecheck clean), bun test 5004 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, lint, typecheck and lore check exit 0. Delivered under opum-control job-08oqbc8w.
